auto_merge.commit_message:
Other (squashed) commits:

fix(tui): emit ui_send output atomically with the frame

Problem:
tui_ui_send() writes directly to the TTY, bypassing the output buffer.
Sequences sent via nvim_ui_send() (e.g. kitty multiple-cursors, or
visual-dot-repeat) always arrive in a separate TTY write from the frame
they were computed for. This manifests as "tearing", or e.g. in the case
of multicursor the terminal renders text with stale cursor overlays.

Solution:
- tui_ui_send(): while a frame is being assembled (pending invalid
  regions or buffered output), buffer instead of writing directly.
  - Out-of-frame sends (tty queries, clear-on-disable) still write
    immediately.
- mcursor.lua: emit the terminal-cursor update at the end of the redraw
  cycle (`on_end`, when screen positions are final) instead of
  vim.schedule().

comment_data.body: This is minor behavior change. For small sequences, it still avoids the begin/end bracket "overhead" described at https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/35406#discussion_r2288851197
`MCursor` hl should probably be something else. maybe link to `Search`, but then that can be confusing if search highlighting is active.

comment_data.body:
I think so too. My initial thoughts are:

- Link to `Cursor`. In the end, these are all cursors. There is a single "true one", of course, which will be somewhat confusing to quickly spot. But I currently think (after trying it in practice for a bit) that this is not the big deal: 1) there are other ways to see where cursor is ('cursorline', 'ruler', statusline, etc.); 2) the multicursor session is probably relatively short lived.
- Make it inverted with `gui=reverse`. The logic is that cursors should be visible.

I think I'd prefer it be linked to `Cursor` by default.

I found the prior `Q` mapping pretty useful and use it often. We should keep this is a default binding, even if it's not still `Q`.

This is a breaking change btw and should probably be listed as such in news.txt.
